title: AbleWave + Redwood: reseller & technical onboarding discovery
summary: Introductory scoping between AbleWave (reseller) and Redwood to understand integration patterns, security requirements, pilot sizing, and go-to-market steps. Discussed Hosted vs Dedicated routing, marketplace listing, SSO/SAML & audit logs, trial benchmarks, and partner margins. Agreed on a technical workshop and to share security docs and an integration checklist.
next_steps: Redwood to send partner integration checklist and security pack (Jordan)
Schedule 2-hour technical workshop with AbleWave infra team (Maya)
AbleWave to share typical customer workload profiles and target latency/SLA (Evan)
Exchange initial pricing / margin sheet for reseller channel (Jordan)
Set up a 2-week pilot template with 100k tokens/day baseline (Samir)
action_items: Jordan Patel: send security pack + SOC2 summary by 2027-02-20
Maya Chen: prepare workshop agenda and runbook by 2027-02-22
Evan Kim: export sample traffic profile and 95th percentile latency targets by 2027-02-24
transcript:
Meeting Header - 2027-02-17 15:00 UTC | Duration 48m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Leo (Redwood Solutions), Priya (AbleWave Head Partnerships), Evan (AbleWave CTO), Samir (AbleWave Lead Eng)

Summary (auto): quick intro to partnership model, technical gating items for reseller marketplace listing, initial pilot sizing, and security/compliance validation.

00:00 - Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, uh, really excited to kick off with AbleWave, uh Priya, thanks for coordinating.
00:12 - Priya: yeah thanks Jordan, happy to be here, we've been looking at Redwood for a bit, the routing and dedicated capacity stuff looks promising for our customers.
00:21 - Maya: quick intro from my side, I'm Maya, I'm the solutions engineer, I'll run the deep technical workshop and the pilot runbooks with you.
00:29 - Evan: awesome, Evan here, CTO, I'll mostly be focused on how we integrate in our marketplace and the VPC/policy requirements.
00:37 - Samir: Samir, lead platform, I'll own the onboarding and benchmarks.
00:42 - Leo: Leo, partner ops, will handle go-to-market enablement and partner portal flows.

02:10 - Jordan: high level, we do three modes: hosted API for quick onboarding, dedicated pools for reserved throughput, and private / VPC for on-prem or regulated customers. Which of those map to your typical offering?
02:22 - Priya: most of our channel customers are SaaS firms that want self-serve hosted, but we get a decent chunk that ask for VPCs or dedicated because they have compliance needs. So we need documentation for both, and a clear story on when to push hosted vs dedicated.
02:36 - Jordan: yeah, makes sense. On the pricing side we have usage-based for hosted and committed monthly for dedicated. For resellers we do a margin sheet plus co-sell credits; we'll share that.
02:50 - Priya: perfect. Also, marketplace listing — do you support a partner SKU or do we route through our own billing?
02:59 - Maya: two options: you can list via partner SKU through our marketplace, or you can route calls to your tenant and we invoice you. Both are supported, tradeoffs on attribution and billing reconciliation.

05:05 - Evan: technical gating question: SSO, SAML, RBAC, audit logs — we need to know what you expose for audit and also KMS/HSM key management because several customers insist on CMEK.
05:18 - Maya: we support SSO with SAML and OIDC, RBAC at route and token level, and we can integrate with customer KMS via our private deployment offering. For hosted customers we offer envelope encryption and bring-your-own-key via our KMS integrations.
05:38 - Samir: when you say persistent logs, are those exportable to Splunk/Datadog and do you keep queryable audit trails per token?
05:46 - Maya: logs can be streamed to your SIEM, and we provide per-request traces in the console; audit retention is configurable based on plan. I'll attach the logs export doc.

07:12 - Jordan: one question we often get: latency vs cost tradeoffs. For inference heavy customers we recommend dedicated with model quantization and batching optimization. For low-latency interactive apps we suggest hosting on our low-latency tiers.
07:32 - Evan: curious about batching — how aggressive is your batching? Our apps are mixed, some chat, some embeddings, so we don't want the batching to add jitter for chat.
07:43 - Maya: we do continuous batching with latency SLOs; you can pin routes to low-latency pool that uses smaller batch windows. There's also KV cache and prefix caching to avoid repeat tokens.
07:58 - Samir: note, sometimes those terms get fuzzy in notes, our security team calls KV cache 'K V cash' and we have to re-explain.
08:05 - (laughter)

10:00 - Priya: on the reseller flow: how do you handle customer onboarding flows — do we create sub-tenants for our customers or do they self-sign through AbleWave's marketplace page?
10:12 - Leo: great operational question; we support both. For marketplace listing we can provision partner-managed sub-tenants and give you admin controls, or you can let customers self-serve and we bill through the partner SKU.
10:28 - Priya: for our first pilot we'd prefer partner-managed so we can control rollout and support.

12:20 - Evan: pilot sizing — we usually need a 2-week pilot. What are standard guardrails you expect for a partner pilot? tokens/day, models, SLOs?
12:33 - Maya: typical baseline we propose is 100k tokens/day with one model variant, 95th percentile latency target documented. We can scale up if the workload needs it. For dedicated capacity we will recommend GPU types and quantization.
12:50 - Samir: can you share examples of GPU sizing for Llama-2 style models? We have a few customers asking for on-prem inference of larger LLMs.
13:02 - Maya: yes, we typically reference A100/RTX 6000 or equivalents; for quantized variants 80% fewer memory needs often. We'll attach a sizing guide; there's also a table in the partner docs.

15:05 - Priya: security review — do you have SOC2 and ISO audits? Customers will ask.
15:11 - Jordan: yes, SOC2 Type II in 2025, ISO27001 certification, and we have pen test reports that we can share under NDA.
15:21 - Evan: great, can you share those and your data residency options? Some EU customers need European-only regions.
15:29 - Jordan: we have regional control and Private deployments can be on-prem or in customer VPCs; we'll share the region availability matrix.

17:40 - Samir: integration specifics: is there an SDK for control plane operations to create keys and route policies programmatically? We need to automate tenant provisioning.
17:50 - Maya: yes, we have REST APIs and SDKs (Python/Go/Node) that allow tenant provisioning, route creation, and policy management. We also have a partner portal API to create partner-managed subtenants.

20:00 - Evan: about fallbacks — if a dedicated pool is saturated what's the typical strategy? Backfill to hosted? degrade gracefully?
20:10 - Maya: smart routing lets you fallback to hosted or lower-cost variant models; there's also canary and A/B flows. You can configure automatic fallback thresholds.
20:22 - Samir: any cold-starts or KV cache warm-up concerns for large models?
20:30 - Maya: KV cache warm-up happens on first request; for predictable latency we recommend warm-up sequences during pilot; we can pre-fill caches for pilot traffic.

22:40 - Priya: go-to-market: what enablement do you provide? co-marketing, technical collateral, joint webinars?
22:48 - Leo: we provide partner decks, playbooks, joint PR templates, and joint webinar support. We also have a partner tier with co-sell credits.

25:00 - Evan: question: can AbleWave route customer traffic through our own edge and then onto Redwood, or must traffic go direct? For compliance we sometimes proxy through our network.
25:12 - Maya: you can proxy through your edge; we support partner-managed routing. We'll need to validate TLS certs and token flows; that's in the integration checklist.

27:30 - Jordan: let's talk about metrics we track: per-route token counts, 95/99 latencies, error rates, and cost per 1k tokens. We also surface quality regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
27:45 - Samir: that quality monitoring—can it be scoped per partner route? We want to own signal and alerts for our marketplace customers.
27:53 - Maya: yes, you can configure per-route alerts and webhook hooks to send to your monitoring stack.

30:05 - Priya: any blockers you foresee for listing us as a reseller? certifications, MSA?
30:13 - Jordan: standard MSA and reseller addendum; security docs and a quick compliance intake. No heavy blockers. We usually require a pilot and a technical workshop pre-listing.

32:00 - Evan: curious about cost controls — do you provide token quotas and alerts to prevent runaway spend by end customers?
32:09 - Maya: we expose quotas, soft and hard limits, and per-API token caps. Partners can set credit thresholds and auto-suspend to manage risk.

34:12 - Samir: about model management—if we want to pin a route to a specific quantized variant, is that done at route config?
34:20 - Maya: yes, pinning at route or tenant level. You can also set auto-rollout policies with canary percentages.

36:00 - Priya: marketing ops — we want a sandbox tile in your partner console so our sales reps can demo quickly.
36:08 - Leo: yep, partner sandbox tenants are supported; we can pre-provision demo tokens and sample prompts.

38:20 - Evan: two technical asks for the workshop: 1) deep dive on KV cache and warm-up sequences, 2) benchmark runbook for throughput vs latency with sample load tests.
38:32 - Maya: noted — we'll prepare a 2-hour workshop covering those and run the baseline benchmark scripts.

40:40 - Samir: do you have a small sample benchmark harness we can run in our environment to compare?
40:46 - Maya: yes, we have a repo with load harness and instructions; will share link. It supports both hosted and dedicated endpoint tests.

42:00 - Jordan: closing — recap: send security pack, integration checklist, pricing/margin sheet, schedule workshop, partner portal access for AbleWave.
42:10 - Priya: sounds good, we aim to have pilot customers lined up in two weeks.
42:18 - Evan: thanks everyone.
42:22 - Jordan: thanks, we'll follow up with docs and calendar invites.

43:00 - (meeting ends)
transcription_notes: occasional speaker label swaps (Jordan/Maya sometimes merged)
ambient cross-talk at 08:05 and 36:00, minor ASR mis-hearings (K V cash instead of KV cache)
some product names normalized for readability
